definitions.explanation: A road within a city or town, especially one lined with buildings or trees. More formal than {道|みち} or {通|とお}り, and often used in urban planning or literary contexts.

examples.japanese: {街路|がいろ}に{沿|そ}って{桜|さくら}が{植|う}えてある。
examples.english: Cherry trees are planted along the street.

examples.japanese: {街路|がいろ}{樹|じゅ}の{落|お}ち{葉|ば}が{歩道|ほどう}を{覆|おお}っている。
examples.english: Fallen leaves from the roadside trees are covering the sidewalk.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}い{街路|がいろ}を{整備|せいび}して、{歩行者|ほこうしゃ}{専用|せんよう}の{遊歩道|ゆうほどう}に{生|う}まれ{変|か}わらせる{計画|けいかく}が{進|すす}んでいる。
examples.english: Plans are underway to renovate old city streets and transform them into pedestrian-only promenades.

notes:
USAGE:
{街路|がいろ} is a somewhat formal word for streets within a city, commonly seen in compound words. It is more specific than {道|みち} (road, path) or {通|とお}り (street, avenue) and carries an urban connotation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {街路|がいろ}{樹|じゅ} (roadside tree, street tree)
- {街路|がいろ}{灯|とう} (street light)
- {街路|がいろ}を{歩|ある}く (walk along a street)
- {街路|がいろ}の{整備|せいび} (street maintenance/improvement)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {道|みち}: road, path (general, any kind of route)
- {通|とお}り: street, avenue (common, everyday word)
- {道路|どうろ}: road (official/administrative term)
